article_title: Blood Transfusion Knowledge among Nurses in Malaysia: A University Hospital Experience.
citation: Mohd Noor Noor Haslina, Saad Noor Hafiza, Khan Mohammad, Hassan Mohd Nazri, Ramli Marini, Bahar Rosnah, Mohamed Yusoff Shafini, Iberahim Salfarina, Wan Ab Rahman Wan Suriana, Zulkafli Zefarina, Islam Md Asiful. (2021). Blood Transfusion Knowledge among Nurses in Malaysia: A University Hospital Experience. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph182111194
title: Modified Routine Blood Transfusion Knowledge Questionnaire (RBTKQ)
description: The RBTKQ is a 43-item questionnaire in seven sections used to assess nurses' blood transfusion knowledge, covering demographics and training, blood bag collection and patient preparation, pre- and post-transfusion nursing responsibilities, complications, and hospital policy. The article used a modified version with "a good reliability score of 68.3 based on the Flesch Reading Ease Index", a maximum score of 56 points, and scoring bands of <50%, 50–74%, and ≥75% for poor, moderate, and high knowledge.
requirements: Requires correct-response scoring with 1 point per item, 5 points for the multi-step patient identification item, and no points for conflicting responses
constraints: The authors note certain aspects of transfusion, such as signs and symptoms of AHTR like back or kidney pain, may have been overlooked by this questionnaire
target_learners: Registered nurses involved in blood transfusion procedures
target_learning_goals: Blood transfusion knowledge including patient preparation, pre- and post-transfusion responsibilities, complications, and policy
examples: Administered to 200 registered nurses at Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia in a cross-sectional survey

The Routines-Based Model Internationally Implemented. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17228308
title: RBI Plus: Routines-Based Interview with ecomap, participation-based child goals, and family goals
description: RBI Plus is the needs-assessment and intervention-planning package that all implementers adopted. It consists of the Routines-Based Interview accompanied by "an ecomap (depicting a family's informal, intermediate, and formal supports), participation-based goals for children, and family goals for siblings and parents." The RBI "is a needs assessment and typically results in 10–12 goals/outcomes," a long list of family-chosen goals the authors call one of the hallmarks of the model. Functional goals are written with criteria for acquisition, generalization, and maintenance.
requirements: An early interventionist trained to conduct the RBI with fidelity
constraints: In Portugal, mixing the RBM into a broader manual diluted the effect of the model
target_learners: Families of young children with disabilities in early intervention
target_learning_goals: Family-chosen functional goals for child participation in routines and family needs
examples: In one Singapore agency, the ecomap and RBI are the most widely adopted components of the RBM
